note.explanation: Permanent magnets are used in devices and everyday tasks. In an A.C. generator, a rotating coil in the magnetic field of a permanent magnet produces an induced emf. In a loudspeaker, a changing current in the voice coil interacts with the magnet’s field, making the cone vibrate and produce sound.
examples: A.C. generator: a coil rotates between the poles of a permanent magnet.
Loudspeaker: the voice coil and attached cone move back and forth.
note.checkAnswer: The changing magnetic field through the rotating coil induces an emf.
note.simple: A permanent magnet can help make electricity in a generator or help make sound in a loudspeaker.
note.checkQuestion: What produces the induced emf in an A.C. generator?
note.title: Uses of Permanent Magnets
steps: In an A.C. generator, rotate a coil between the poles of a permanent magnet.
The magnetic field through the coil changes.
An emf is induced between the ends of the coil.
When the ends are connected to an external circuit, alternating current flows.
note.answer: Permanent magnets are used in generators and loudspeakers, as well as in door catchers, refrigerator door strips, flourmills, medical tools for removing iron splinters, and resetting the pointer in a maximum and minimum thermometer.

options: The magnetic field through the coil changes
The coil becomes a permanent magnet
The coil stops rotating
The magnet loses all its poles
mcqs.stem: In an A.C. generator, why is an emf induced when a coil is rotated between the poles of a permanent magnet?
rationales: Correct: rotation changes the magnetic field through the coil, inducing an emf.
Incorrect: the coil does not need to become a permanent magnet to generate an emf.
Incorrect: the coil must rotate for the magnetic field through it to change.
Incorrect: the permanent magnet’s poles do not disappear during normal generator operation.

options: A.C. flows in the external circuit
Only D.C. flows in the external circuit
No current flows
The circuit becomes a permanent magnet
mcqs.stem: What type of current flows through an external circuit connected to the rotating coil of an A.C. generator?
rationales: Correct: the induced current is alternating current when the coil ends are connected to an external circuit.
Incorrect: the section describes alternating current, not only direct current.
Incorrect: a current flows when the coil ends are connected to an external circuit.
Incorrect: connecting a generator does not turn the circuit into a permanent magnet.

options: A voice coil in the gap of a permanent magnet
A steel bar placed inside a refrigerator
A compass needle beside a loudspeaker
A permanent magnet attached to a microphone cone
mcqs.stem: Which arrangement is used in the moving-coil loudspeaker described in this section?
rationales: Correct: the voice coil is inserted in the gap of the permanent magnet and attached to the cone.
Incorrect: a steel bar in a refrigerator is not the loudspeaker arrangement described.
Incorrect: a compass needle is not the part that produces the speaker’s sound.
Incorrect: the voice coil is attached to the cone, not the permanent magnet.

options: The cone vibrates back and forth
The cone stays still while the magnet rotates
The microphone cone attracts iron nails
The permanent magnet produces sound by itself
mcqs.stem: How does a moving-coil loudspeaker produce sound in the air?
rationales: Correct: the varying force moves the voice coil and cone back and forth, producing sound.
Incorrect: the cone moves; the section does not describe a rotating magnet.
Incorrect: attracting iron nails is not the speaker’s sound-producing action.
Incorrect: the magnet alone does not produce the sound described.

options: To keep the refrigerator door closed tightly
To make the refrigerator colder by itself
To remove all the air from the refrigerator
To generate alternating current for the refrigerator
mcqs.stem: What is the purpose of the magnetic strips fitted to refrigerator and freezer doors?
rationales: Correct: the strips help keep the doors closed tightly.
Incorrect: the strips do not cool the refrigerator.
Incorrect: the strips do not remove air from the refrigerator.
Incorrect: the strips are door seals, not generators.

options: To remove iron nails from grains before grinding
To turn grains into iron
To make the flour magnetic
To grind the grains without a mill
mcqs.stem: Why do flourmills use permanent magnets before grinding grains?
rationales: Correct: the magnets remove iron objects such as nails from the grains.
Incorrect: a magnet does not turn grains into iron.
Incorrect: the purpose is to remove iron objects, not make flour magnetic.
Incorrect: magnets do not replace the grinding process.

written.text: Q8.4. Name some uses of permanent magnets and electromagnets.
written.finalAnswer: Permanent magnets are used in D.C. motors, A.C. and D.C. generators, moving-coil loudspeakers, door catchers, refrigerator and freezer door strips, flourmills to remove iron objects, medical tools to remove iron splinters from eyes, and to reset the pointer in a maximum and minimum thermometer. example.question: Describe how an A.C. generator uses a permanent magnet to produce current.
example.answer: A coil rotated between the poles of a permanent magnet experiences a changing magnetic field through it. An emf is induced between its ends, and when they are connected to an external circuit, alternating current flows.

explain.title: Everyday and practical uses
explain.body: Permanent magnets are used in motors and generators, loudspeakers, door catchers, refrigerator and freezer door strips, flourmills, medical tools for removing iron splinters, and resetting the pointer in a maximum and minimum thermometer.

explain.title: A.C. generator
explain.body: When a coil rotates between the poles of a permanent magnet, the magnetic field through the coil changes. This induces an emf. If the coil ends are connected to an external circuit, alternating current flows.

explain.title: Moving-coil loudspeaker
explain.body: A varying A.C. passes through the voice coil in the gap of a permanent magnet. The current interacts with the magnetic field and produces a varying force. This pushes and pulls the voice coil and cone, causing the cone to vibrate and produce sound.

explain.title: How to describe the device
explain.body: For a generator, link coil rotation to changing magnetic field, induced emf, and current. For a loudspeaker, link varying current to force, cone vibration, and sound.

mistakes: Do not say that a generator produces current just because a magnet is present; the coil must rotate so the magnetic field through it changes.
Do not confuse emf induced in the coil with current flowing in the external circuit: current flows when the coil ends are connected to that circuit.
Do not say that the permanent magnet itself makes the loudspeaker cone vibrate; the varying current in the voice coil interacts with the magnetic field.
Do not leave out the cone’s back-and-forth vibration when explaining how a loudspeaker produces sound.
